function.name: done
function.arguments: {"summary": "Picked up the red block from the table and transported it to the blue bowl. After visual servoing I grasped the block (gripper reading ~0.55 while held), lifted, carried it ~14 cm to the bowl, lowered it into the opening and released it. The block landed at the bowl near-inner slope, so I pressed it down with the closed fingers to seat it inside the bowl. Final views show the block at the bowl near-interior with part of it visible inside the bowl opening; it may still be leaning against the inner wall rather than resting flat on the bowl floor.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts about this rig: (1) The wrist camera looks down tilted toward +x (the bowl side): image-up corresponds to +x, the finger-separation axis is image-horizontal (about y), and objects directly below the gripper appear near the frame bottom; the wrist image rotates with commanded yaw. (2) move_to calls that only change Cartesian targets execute only 2-4 control steps (~1-1.5 cm of travel) per decision, but calls that include a gripper open/close transition run 39-80 steps and advance the Cartesian motion along with the servo - pair long transports with a gripper transition. (3) A yaw command swings the TCP sideways roughly 7-13 cm per radian during the motion; avoid large yaw changes near objects. (4) The eef_pos reference sits about 4 cm above the fingertip plane: over the table the descent stalls near TCP z=0.843, and a 4 cm block is grasped with the TCP around 0.84. (5) This trial layout: block near (-0.075, 0.002), bowl opening near (0.065-0.08, 0.0) with the rim around z=0.86-0.88; releasing from TCP z~0.889 drops the block into the opening. (6) Gripper normalized reading: ~0.99 open, ~0.52-0.57 while holding the block, ~0.11 closed on air."}
